subject: About the efficiency of a three-level poisson regression model

messages.author: 001cf0197468e0b0
messages.subject: About the efficiency of a three-level poisson regression model
parts:
Hi there,

I am a relatively new stan user trying to utilize this great tool for real applications.

I am fitting a very simple poisson regression model with three levels. An example is that hotels (Level 3) will receive 5 different kinds of ratings (Level2), and these ratings can be repeated on each day (Level3). 

The model could be:
y_{ivl} ~ poisson(rate_{ivl})
log(rate_{ivl})  =  \lambda_{vl} + \beta_{1 vl}*x_{1 ivl} + ... + \beta_{P vl} * x_{P ivl}

We assume the \lambda_{l} ~ Multivariate Normal(\mu_L, \Sigma) to account for the heterogeneity in the second level, and \beta_{p vl }~ Uni-variate Normal (\mu_{p v}, \sigma_{p v}) for the heterogeneous covariates effects. Those multi-variate and uni-variate random effects of interest.

I have read the example on hierarchical model in the Stan manual 2.9 (PP. 70 - PP. 75) and follow the coding advise, but the result is a little disappointing. I have done all the vectoring, transformation suggested in the manual. However, the inference costs over 40 minutes with 2,000 simulated samples for each second level (total 10,000 samples). I noticed that reduce the warm-up size or lower the adapt_delta boost the speed, yet the estimation for the random effects are not at all accurate.  In the real data, there are over 400,000 samples. I do not know how many months do I need for the inference.   

Here I attach the simulation R code and stan code as follows:

R code:

set.seed(11)
if(!require(mvtnorm))
install.packages(pkgs="mvtnorm",repos="http://cran.r-project.org")
library(mvtnorm)

N1 = 2000
N2 = 2000
N3 = 2000
N4 = 2000
N5 = 2000

L = 200
V = 5
P = 5
Lambda = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = V)
Beta1 = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = P)
Beta2 = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = P)
Beta3 = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = P)
Beta4 = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = P)
Beta5 = matrix(0,nrow = L, ncol = P)

Mu = c(0.4,-0.4,0.4,-0.4,0.4)
Sigma = c(0.25,0.6,0.25,0.6,0.25)
Mu_L = c(-4,-8,-4,-8,-4)
Sigma_L = matrix(c(1.0, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3
                  ,0.3, 1.0, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3
                  ,0.3, 0.3, 1.0, 0.3, 0.3
                  ,0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0, 0.3
                  ,0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 1.0), nrow=5)
Xcov1 = matrix(rnorm(N1*P),nrow = N1,ncol = P)
Xcov2 = matrix(rnorm(N2*P),nrow = N2,ncol = P)
Xcov3 = matrix(rnorm(N3*P),nrow = N3,ncol = P)
Xcov4 = matrix(rnorm(N4*P),nrow = N4,ncol = P)
Xcov5 = matrix(rnorm(N5*P),nrow = N5,ncol = P)
for(j in 1:L){
Beta1[j,] = rnorm(P,mean = Mu, sd = Sigma)
Beta2[j,] = rnorm(P,mean = Mu, sd = Sigma)
Beta3[j,] = rnorm(P,mean = Mu, sd = Sigma)
Beta4[j,] = rnorm(P,mean = Mu, sd = Sigma)
Beta5[j,] = rnorm(P,mean = Mu, sd = Sigma)
Lambda[j,] = rmvnorm(1,mean = Mu_L, sigma = Sigma_L)
}
LL1 = rep(seq(L),N1/L)
LL2 = rep(seq(L),N2/L)
LL3 = rep(seq(L),N3/L)
LL4 = rep(seq(L),N4/L)
LL5 = rep(seq(L),N5/L)

Y1 = rep(0, N1)
Y2 = rep(0, N2)
Y3 = rep(0, N3)
Y4 = rep(0, N4)
Y5 = rep(0, N5)
for(i in 1:N1){
Y1[i] = rpois(1,lambda = exp(Lambda[LL1[i],1] + sum(Xcov1[i,]*Beta1[LL1[i],])))
}
for(i in 1:N2){
Y2[i] = rpois(1,lambda = exp(Lambda[LL2[i],2] + sum(Xcov2[i,]*Beta2[LL2[i],])))
}
for(i in 1:N3){
Y3[i] = rpois(1,lambda = exp(Lambda[LL3[i],3] + sum(Xcov3[i,]*Beta3[LL3[i],])))
}
for(i in 1:N4){
Y4[i] = rpois(1,lambda = exp(Lambda[LL4[i],4] + sum(Xcov4[i,]*Beta4[LL4[i],])))
}
for(i in 1:N5){
Y5[i] = rpois(1,lambda = exp(Lambda[LL5[i],5] + sum(Xcov5[i,]*Beta5[LL5[i],])))
}


u = rep(1,L)

time_start = Sys.time()
library(rstan)
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

pois_dat = list(N1 = N1, N2 = N2, N3 = N3, N4 = N4, N5 = N5, L = L,  P = P, Y1 = Y1, Y2 = Y2, Y3 = Y3, Y4 = Y4, Y5 = Y5, Xcov1 = Xcov1, Xcov2 = Xcov2, Xcov3 = Xcov3, Xcov4 = Xcov4, Xcov5 = Xcov5, LL1 = LL1, LL2 = LL2, LL3 = LL3, LL4 = LL4, LL5 = LL5, u = u)
fit <- stan(file = "2try_poisson.stan",data = pois_dat, iter = 1000,warmup = 300, pars = c("Mu1","Mu2","Mu3","Mu4","Mu5","Sigma1","Sigma2","Sigma3","Sigma4","Sigma5","Mu_L","tau"), chains = 2, control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95))
print(fit,par = c("Mu1","Mu2","Mu3","Mu4","Mu5","Sigma1","Sigma2","Sigma3","Sigma4","Sigma5","Mu_L","tau"))

time_end = Sys.time()
print(time_end - time_start)

============================================
stan code:

data {
int<lower=0> N1; //total sample size for rating 1
int<lower=0> N2; //total sample size rating 2
int<lower=0> N3; //total sample size rating 3
int<lower=0> N4; //total sample size rating 4
int<lower=0> N5; //total sample size rating 5
int<lower=1> L; //levels, number of hotels
int<lower=0> P; //total covariates, 5
int<lower = 0> Y1[N1]; //count outcomes
int<lower = 0> Y2[N2]; //count outcomes
int<lower = 0> Y3[N3]; //count outcomes
int<lower = 0> Y4[N4]; //count outcomes
int<lower = 0> Y5[N5]; //count outcomes
row_vector[P] Xcov1[N1]; //covariates
row_vector[P] Xcov2[N2]; //covariates
row_vector[P] Xcov3[N3]; //covariates
row_vector[P] Xcov4[N4]; //covariates
row_vector[P] Xcov5[N5]; //covariates
int<lower = 1> LL1[N1]; //which hotel
int<lower = 1> LL2[N2];
int<lower = 1> LL3[N3];
int<lower = 1> LL4[N4];
int<lower = 1> LL5[N5];
vector[L] u; // all elements to be 1
}
parameters {
vector[P] beta1[L];
vector[P] beta2[L];
vector[P] beta3[L];
vector[P] beta4[L];
vector[P] beta5[L];
real Mu1[P];
real Mu2[P];
real Mu3[P];
real Mu4[P];
real Mu5[P];
real<lower = 0.001> Sigma1[P];
real<lower = 0.001> Sigma2[P];
real<lower = 0.001> Sigma3[P];
real<lower = 0.001> Sigma4[P];
real<lower = 0.001> Sigma5[P];
row_vector[5] Mu_L; // mean for the multivariate random effect
vector<lower=0>[5] tau;  
cholesky_factor_corr[5] L_omega;
matrix[5,L] z;
}
transformed parameters {
  matrix[L,5] lambda;
  lambda <- u*Mu_L + (diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_omega) * z)';
}

model{
   vector[N1] x_beta1;
   vector[N2] x_beta2;
   vector[N3] x_beta3;
   vector[N4] x_beta4;
   vector[N5] x_beta5;
   
   for(i in 1:N1){
x_beta1[i] <- exp(lambda[LL1[i],1] + Xcov1[i]*beta1[LL1[i]]);
}
for(i in 1:N2){
x_beta2[i] <- exp(lambda[LL2[i],2] + Xcov2[i]*beta2[LL2[i]]);
}
for(i in 1:N3){
x_beta3[i] <- exp(lambda[LL3[i],3] + Xcov3[i]*beta3[LL3[i]]);
}
for(i in 1:N4){
x_beta4[i] <- exp(lambda[LL4[i],4] + Xcov4[i]*beta4[LL4[i]]);
}
for(i in 1:N5){
x_beta5[i] <- exp(lambda[LL5[i],5] + Xcov5[i]*beta5[LL5[i]]);
}
   for(l in 1:L){
 beta1[l] ~ normal(Mu1,Sigma1);
 beta2[l] ~ normal(Mu2,Sigma2);
 beta3[l] ~ normal(Mu3,Sigma3);
 beta4[l] ~ normal(Mu4,Sigma4);
 beta5[l] ~ normal(Mu5,Sigma5);
}
Mu1~normal(0,1);
Sigma1~cauchy(0,1);
Mu2~normal(0,1);
Sigma2~cauchy(0,1);
Mu3~normal(0,1);
Sigma3~cauchy(0,1);
Mu4~normal(0,1);
Sigma4~cauchy(0,1);
Mu5~normal(0,1);
Sigma5~cauchy(0,1);
Y1~poisson(x_beta1);
Y2~poisson(x_beta2);
Y3~poisson(x_beta3);
Y4~poisson(x_beta4);
Y5~poisson(x_beta5);
to_vector(z) ~ normal(0,1);
L_omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
Mu_L ~ normal(0,1);
tau ~ cauchy(0,1);
}

The code is in the similar form (I think! XD) suggested in the manual. I am curious whether the code or my simulation setting can be improved.

Thank you very very much for the help in advance.

Best regards,
Xiangnan

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] About the efficiency of a three-level poisson regression model
parts: You want to vectorize everything, like

First, you want to define log_x_beta5 (no exp()) and

x_beta5 <- lambda[LL5, 5] + Xcov5 .* beta5[LL5];

That won't save you much speed --- just some typing.

then use the poisson_log() distribution (parameter on
the log scale).

You can also flatten this out, but with so many varying
Sigma, it's still not going to be efficient

You might be able to get away with less heavy-tailed priors
than the Cauchy, too.

Are all your parameters roughly on a unit scale?

You shouldn't need lower=0.001 for scale parameters.

But overall, Stan's not reallyd esigned for big data applications
with super complex models.

If your model takes more than 2K iterations to converge, there
are probably bigger problems with redundancy in parameterization, etc.
Those might save you, because 400K isn't out of the question as
far as data size goes, even in a complex model.

- Bob
